title: Investigatio motuum, quibus laminae et virgae elasticae contremiscunt

deep.reconstruction: Problem (§35): find every vibration of an elastic rod whose two ends E and F are both 'simply fixed' (pinned, or simply supported, in modern terms). Euler earlier separated variables in the beam equation, which in modern form is y_tt + K y_ssss = 0. He took y = sin(ζ + νt)·Y(s), so the spatial factor satisfies Y'''' = Y/f^4, where the constant f is tied to the frequency. Its general solution is Y = α e^{s/f} + β e^{-s/f} + γ sin(s/f) + δ cos(s/f). Pinned-end conditions are Y = 0 (no displacement) and Y'' = 0 (no bending moment) at s = 0 and at s = a. At s = 0: α+β+δ = 0 and α+β−δ = 0. Hence δ = 0 and β = −α. Write ω = a/f. At s = a: α e^ω + β e^{-ω} + γ sin ω + δ cos ω = 0 and α e^ω + β e^{-ω} − γ sin ω − δ cos ω = 0. Substituting gives α(e^ω − e^{-ω}) + γ sin ω = 0 and α(e^ω − e^{-ω}) − γ sin ω = 0. Their sum gives 2α·2sinh ω = 0, so α = 0 for ω ≠ 0. Their difference gives 2γ sin ω = 0. Taking γ = 0 would leave the rod at rest, so sin ω = 0 and ω = nπ. On the next page the frequencies come out proportional to ω², i.e. to n²π² c√(2gb)/a², so the partials rise as the squares 1, 4, 9, 16. The modes are sin(nπu), the same shapes as a vibrating string, with n−1 interior nodes. The general motion is a superposition Σ C_n sin(ζ_n + n²π² c√(2gb) t/a²) sin(nπu). This is the fourth case of Euler's systematic classification of end conditions (free, clamped, pinned) for the transverse vibration of rods.
errors: Printed typo in the second reduced equation: 'γ sin. α ω' should read 'γ sin. ω'. The 'α' is spurious, and the subsequent sum and difference use sin ω correctly.
Minor: the conclusion α = 0 needs ω ≠ 0 (sinh ω ≠ 0). Euler handles this implicitly by treating ω = 0 as the state of rest on the next page.

ideas.what: Separation of variables for the Euler–Bernoulli beam equation, with general spatial solution e^{±s/f}, sin(s/f), cos(s/f)
ideas.modern_name: Normal modes of the Euler–Bernoulli beam
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler and Daniel Bernoulli (1735–1744); systematised by Euler in E526
ideas.where_published: E526 itself; earlier the Additamentum I (De curvis elasticis) to the Methodus inveniendi (1744)

ideas.what: Pinned–pinned boundary conditions y = 0, y'' = 0, giving the frequency equation sin ω = 0, ω = nπ, frequencies ∝ n², and sine mode shapes identical to those of a string
ideas.modern_name: Simply supported beam eigenvalues ω_n = nπ, f_n ∝ n²
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E526, presented 1774, published 1782); also treated in Rayleigh's Theory of Sound
ideas.where_published: E526 §35–36; discussed in Truesdell's 'Rational mechanics of flexible or elastic bodies' (Opera omnia II 11₂)

ideas.what: Fourier-type superposition of all simple modes as the general motion
ideas.modern_name: Modal expansion / Fourier sine series solution
ideas.where_published: E526; earlier Euler papers on vibrating strings

deep.surprise_reason: This is the textbook pinned–pinned beam case, correctly solved. The paper's results are well documented by Truesdell in the Opera omnia commentary. Apart from a printing typo, nothing on this page is new or uncredited.
transcription_corrections: The transcription faithfully reproduces the printed 'γ sin. α ω'; the image indeed shows this. Mathematically it should be 'γ sin. ω' (printer's error).
The second reduced equation in the image reads α(e^ω − e^{−ω}) − γ sin. α ω = 0, consistent with the transcription; no other discrepancies noted.
